audit_notes: Model: Pasternak foundation (shear-stiff crust G_c t_c on a Winkler gel k = E_gel/t_gel) under a Gaussian strip load of width a and peak p (integral p*a per unit length), symmetric at x=0, deflection decayed at x = H = 15 mm (3.3 spreading lengths). Spreading length l = sqrt(G_c t_c/k) = sqrt(1500/7.2e7) = 4.6 mm; for a << l the peak gel stress is k w(0) ~ p a/(2 l) = 5e5*3e-4/9.1e-3 = 16 kPa, i.e. a 30x reduction relative to the applied bristle pressure. Baseline choice: comparing with a standard foul-release coating on stress alone would be misleading (standard silicone is stiffer and ~10x stronger than a soft gel), so the baseline is the nilas-crust elite this concept is derived from (crust 0.15 mm, G 0.5 MPa -> G_c t_c = 75 N/m, l = 1.0 mm): peak gel stress ~ 150/(2*1.02e-3) = 74 kPa. Expected gain ~78% lower peak gel stress under point loads. Relevance: gel cohesive strength ~0.05-0.1 MPa, so the parent would be at the damage threshold under a 0.5 MPa bristle and the new crust keeps it at ~20% of strength - a meaningful durability gain for in-water grooming. For blunt fender loads (a = 50 mm >> l) the spreading gives no reduction. Side effect not in the model: the stiffer crust raises the surface compliance-limited release stress (series compliance adds t_c/G_c = 6e-11 m/Pa, negligible in shear, but the bending length for peel grows to ~(D/k)^(1/4) ~ 1.3 mm, still below barnacle size). Drag: 0 (no change of the wetted surface). Solver: the Gaussian source has no simple closed form -> scipy (FDM reference). Dimensionless: a/l = 0.066, H/l = 3.3, crust/gel stiffness ratio G_c t_c/(k l^2) = 1 by definition, peak stress/gel strength ~ 0.2.
